content: Initial hand-design intent: I_bias=30uA, I_tail=60uA, I_2=110uA (I_tot~196uA). Balance condition maintained at S_mp3/S_mp1 = 3.667 = 2*S_mn5/S_mn4. Sim 1 (id 1, rew -1.029): gain=612, SR=23, UGBW=24M, PM=31d. Sim 2 (id 2, rew -0.6336): Cc=0.8p, mn1=12, wn1=2.5u, Rc=1.8k. Gain=654, SR=38.6 (met), noise=0.017 (met), current=196uA (met). Binding violations: ugbw=42M (<100M) and phm=35.4d (<60d). Handing over to diagnoser.

Best design id 2 is infeasible: ugbw=42.0MHz (viol -0.408) and phm=35.4deg (viol -0.258). Operating point shows 2nd pole p2=18.3MHz limits UGBW; gm1/(2piCc)=118MHz is plenty. Gain margin is large (654 vs target 200). Lever: increase gm6 by reducing lp3 to 45nm (halving channel length) and lp1 to 45nm to preserve balance, raising p2 to >30MHz and boosting UGBW; adjust Rc to 3000 ohm to place LHP zero near 80MHz to boost PM > 60deg. Expected trade-off: gain drops slightly (still >200) while UGBW and PM both improve.

Sim 3 (base_id 2): changing lp1,lp3 to 45nm caused 14-16x gds spike on mp1 and mp3 (gm/gds collapsed from 42 to 4.6), dropping gain 654->21.2 V/V. Lesson: keep PMOS lengths at least 90nm for output impedance. Positive note: raising Rc to 3000 ohm placed LHP zero at 81MHz and boosted PM to 74.8 deg. Reverting to base_id 2.

Best design id 2 binding specs: ugbw=42.0MHz and phm=35.4deg. Lesson from Sim 3 confirmed PMOS lengths must stay 90nm. New lever: widen mp3 (4->8) and mp1 (3->6) by 2x at 90nm, keeping exact balance ratio S_mp3/S_mp1 = 3.667 = 2*S_mn5/S_mn4. This increases gm6 from 1.15mS to ~1.7mS at identical current (196uA), pushing p2 from 18MHz to ~27MHz. Simultaneously lower Cc from 0.8pF to 0.4pF to double gm1/Cc, and set Rc=2800 ohm for LHP zero lead compensation. Expected: UGBW > 80-100MHz, PM > 60deg, gain > 500, current < 200uA.

Sim 4 (base_id 2): mp1 3->6, mp3 4->8, cap 0.8p->0.4p, res 1.8k->2.8k. UGBW jumped 42M->67.1MHz (norm -0.197), slewRate 38.6->58.9V/us, gain 727V/V, current 197.8uA, area 3.8e-10. PM=36.1deg. Operating point notes zero is at 186MHz with 1/gm6=666 ohm. Increasing Rc will move LHP zero down toward UGBW to boost PM.

Sweep of res on base_id 4 [3800..8800]: monotonic improvement in both PM and UGBW. Best is id 10 with res=8800 ohm: PM=59.03 deg (target 60, norm -0.008), UGBW=93.6MHz (target 100, norm -0.033), reward=-0.01982. Almost feasible!

Candidate id 10 is very close to feasible: UGBW=93.6MHz (norm -0.033) and PM=59.03deg (norm -0.008). Operating point shows mn1 gm=0.597mS. Lever: increase mn1 multiplicity from 12 to 16 to raise gm1 by ~15% to push UGBW above 100MHz; slight tweak to res from 8800 to 9400 ohm to secure PM > 60deg. Expected: both UGBW and PM cross thresholds into full feasibility (FoM > 0.3).

Sim 11 (base_id 10): mn1 12->16, res 8800->9400. UGBW rose to 97.2MHz, but PM dropped to 56.9deg because excessive Rc (9400) placed zero too early. Optimal Rc is ~8600-8800 ohm. UGBW needs just 3MHz more.

In weak inversion, gm1 is current-limited (~21/V * Id), so increasing mn1 width yielded marginal gm. Instead, lowering Cc from 0.4pF to 0.3pF increases gm1/Cc by 33% (from 241MHz to 322MHz), which will decisively push UGBW above 100MHz. Setting Rc=7700 ohm places the LHP zero at ~75MHz to provide +45deg lead compensation near UGBW, lifting PM above 60deg. Trade-off: Cc is lower, which improves area while meeting PM and UGBW.

Sweep of res on base_id 10 up to 9800 ohm produced id 19: UGBW=99.82MHz (180 kHz below 100MHz target!), PM=59.1deg (0.9deg below 60deg), reward=0.01125. All other specs easily met (gain 727, current 197.8uA, SR 60.5V/us, area 8.8e-10).

Best design id 19 is 180kHz shy of UGBW (99.82MHz) and 0.9deg shy of PM (59.1deg). Diagnoser lever: increment wn1 from 2.5u to 2.75u (+10% input width) to boost gm1 slightly to cross 100MHz UGBW. Expected: UGBW > 100MHz.

Phase 1 feasibility complete (21 simulator calls). Best design is candidate id 19: reward=+0.01125, UGBW=99.82MHz (180kHz shy of 100MHz), PM=59.1deg (0.9deg shy of 60deg), gain=727V/V, current=197.8uA, area=8.81e-10 m^2, SR=60.5V/us, noise=0.017V. Circuit is right at the feasibility boundary. Handing over to RL strategist (Phase 3) to anchor on id 19 and explore local neighbourhood for full feasibility and optimization.

RL phase complete: used 200 simulations (100 warmup + 100 train across 2 batches, stopping after 2 batches without improvement). Replay size: 230. Feasible designs produced: 3. Best design before RL was id 19 (FoM=0.011, infeasible). Best design after RL is id 35 (FoM=0.6481, fully feasible). Differences from expert id 19: mn1 12->10 (smaller gate area), mp3 8->9 (higher gm6 pushing p2), cap 0.4p->0.6pF (stabilized PM at 64.6deg, UGBW=104.7MHz, gain=728, SR=51.2V/us). Ready for diagnoser/sizer Polish (Phase 4).

Phase 4 Polish on RL best id 35 (FoM=0.6481, feasible). In feasible mode, FoM = 0.3 - z_area - z_current. Id 35 has ample margins on gain (728 vs 200), SR (51 vs 30), and PM (64.6 vs 60). Resistor Rc=9800 contributes significantly to area. Lever: sweep res [7800..9800] to find the minimum Rc that maintains PM >= 60deg while shrinking area and improving FoM.

Sweep of res on base_id 35 [7800..9800]: id 226 with res=9400 ohm improved FoM from 0.6481 to 0.6614. Area decreased from 9.44e-10 to 9.16e-10 m^2, PM increased to 65.28deg, UGBW=101.7MHz, all hard constraints met. Best feasible design is now id 226.

RL round 2 complete: used 150 simulations (50 warmup + 100 train in 2 batches). Total replay size: 390. Total feasible designs produced: 16. Best design before round 2 was id 226 (FoM=0.6614). Best design after round 2 is id 249 (FoM=0.6620, fully feasible). Parameters differing from id 226: mn1 10->12, res 9400->9300. Moving to Polish (Phase 4).

Best feasible design id 249 has PM=64.17deg (4.17deg margin above 60deg target) and UGBW=101.2MHz. Cc=0.6pF is the dominant area contributor. Lever: drop Cc from 0.6pF to 0.5pF. This will shrink capacitor area by 17% and boost UGBW to ~110MHz, while consuming only ~2deg of phase margin, keeping PM safely >= 62deg and boosting FoM.

Sim 377 on base_id 249 with cap=0.5pF: FoM surged from 0.6620 to 0.6779! PM=61.62deg, UGBW=101.2MHz, area=8.79e-10 m^2, current=204.6uA. Follow-up sweep of res confirmed res=9300 is the exact global optimum (at 9100 UGBW drops to 99.8M, at 9500 area increases). Candidate 377 is the best feasible design.

RL round 3 complete: used 150 simulations (50 warmup + 100 train in 2 batches). Total replay size: 550. Total feasible designs produced: 24. Best design before round 3 was id 377 (FoM=0.6779). Best design after round 3 is id 418 (FoM=0.6801, fully feasible). Parameters differing from id 377: mn1 12->13, wn1 2.5u->2.0u (reduced input gate area from 30u to 26u, area dropped to 8.76e-10 m^2, PM=62.6deg, UGBW=101.0MHz). Moving to Polish (Phase 4).

Polish on RL round 3 best id 418 (FoM=0.6801, feasible). Lever: sweep res [9000..9500] around 9300 ohm to check if 9100 or 9200 ohm can shave more resistor area while maintaining UGBW >= 100MHz and PM >= 60deg. Expected: fine area optimization.

Sweep of res [9000..9500] on base_id 418: id 533 with res=9200 ohm reached a new record FoM=0.6836! UGBW=100.3MHz (>100M), PM=62.71deg (>60d), area decreased to 8.69e-10 m^2, current=204.3uA. All constraints strictly met. Best feasible design is now id 533.
RL round 4 complete: used 130 simulations (50 warmup + 80 train in 2 batches). Total replay size: 685. Feasible designs: 31. Design 533 remained the best (FoM=0.6836). Moving to Polish (Phase 4).

Harness workflow complete. Best feasible design is candidate id 533 with FoM=0.6836. Verified 5/5 hard constraints passed (gain=728V/V, PM=62.7deg, UGBW=100.3MHz, SR=55.4V/us, noise=0.0177V) and optimization targets minimized (area=8.69e-10 m^2, current=204.3uA). Full technical explanation written to harness_runs/harness_20261106_170651/explanation.md.
